author: @whiskey_lima729
text:
Good morning 🍵🦀🇺🇸

Pre-market overview — Thursday, October 15, 2026 (~5:15 AM EDT)

Futures

U.S. equity futures are mixed to lower, pointing to a cautious open after Wednesday’s tech-led selloff:
•Dow futures: ~+0.3–0.4% (around 52,035–52,057)
•S&P 500 futures: ~−0.25–0.3% (around 7,749–7,751)
•Nasdaq 100 futures: ~−1.0–1.1% (around 29,855–29,863)

Tech remains the clear underperformer. Asia saw a much sharper rout overnight.

Yesterday’s close & drivers
Wall Street finished lower on hotter-than-expected September CPI:
•Nasdaq: −1.9% (worst day since July 23)
•S&P 500: −1.1%
•Dow: −0.1%

Headline CPI rose 0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y (vs. 3.6% expected, up from 3.4% in August). Core came in at 0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y (above forecasts). The print, driven heavily by energy, revived concerns about additional Fed tightening before year-end. Markets are now pricing a higher probability of an October or December hike.

Asia overnight
The AI/tech unwind accelerated:
•South Korea’s Kospi: −7.5% to −8% (SK Hynix and Samsung both down >9–11%)
•Nikkei 225: −4.9%
•Hang Seng and CSI 300 also lower

$CRWV was at the center of the move. Its stock fell ~15% and its bonds moved into distress territory (yields approaching/exceeding 15% on certain 2031/2032 notes). The episode triggered broader selling in AI infrastructure names (Oracle, neoclouds, etc.) on leverage and funding concerns. The CEO later pushed back, citing a large contracted backlog.

Commodities & geopolitics
•WTI: ~$94 (down ~1%)
•Brent: ~$104 (down ~1.7%)
•Gold: rebounding ~+1.2% to the mid-$4,150s as the dollar eased and risk aversion increased

Oil is easing despite ongoing Strait of Hormuz risks (including reports of a ship striking a mine and other vessel attacks). The market is also weighing potential U.S. moves to ease certain sanctions on shadow-fleet vessels, which could improve shipping economics. Energy costs remain a key input into the recent inflation prints.

Today’s calendar (key items at 8:30 AM ET)
•PPI (September) — consensus roughly +0.5–0.6% m/m
•Retail sales (September) — consensus ~+0.3–0.4% m/m
•Initial jobless claims — consensus ~200k
•Earnings from regional banks ($USB , $PNC) and others (including $SCHW )

A hot PPI print would reinforce the inflation/Fed-hike narrative; a softer one could ease some pressure. Retail sales will give a read on consumer resilience after the strong August number.

Bottom line: Tech and AI-related names are under pressure from both hotter inflation data and growing credit/leverage concerns in the data-center buildout. Oil is softening for now despite Hormuz risks, while gold is catching a bid. The 8:30 AM data dump (especially PPI) is the immediate focus for rate expectations.
